draft.title: Meiosis
card: Meiosis is cell division that makes sex cells (gametes), such as sperm and egg cells. One diploid cell divides twice and makes four cells.
Each new cell has half the chromosome number of the parent cell. In humans, a body cell has 46 chromosomes and a gamete has 23.
Crossing over
matching chromosomes swap sections of DNA. This makes new combinations of alleles on a chromosome.
Independent assortment
the pairs of chromosomes line up and separate at random. Each gamete gets a different mix of chromosomes from the two parents.
draft.remember: Meiosis makes four different cells with half the chromosomes, ready for fertilisation.

a.q: A human cell with 46 chromosomes divides by meiosis. What does it make?
opts: Four cells, each with 23 chromosomes
Two cells, each with 23 chromosomes
Four cells, each with 46 chromosomes
Two cells, each with 46 chromosomes
a.why: Meiosis has two divisions, so it makes four cells, and each has half the chromosome number: 23. Two cells with 46 chromosomes is the result of a division that keeps the full number, not meiosis.
a.clue: Meiosis divides twice and halves the number.

b.q: Two sisters have the same parents but are not genetically identical. Which part of meiosis helps explain this?
opts: Chromosome pairs separate at random into each gamete
Each gamete keeps the full chromosome number
Each gamete is a copy of the parent cell
One cell divides once to make two gametes
b.why: Independent assortment gives each gamete a different mix of chromosomes, so each child gets a different combination. The other options describe gametes that would be identical to the parent cell or the wrong number of chromosomes, which would not explain differences.
b.clue: Think about how chromosomes are shared out into gametes.

b.best: Chromosome pairs separate at random into each gamete

problems.detail: The clue 'Meiosis divides twice and halves the number' gives the answer away. Two divisions means four cells, and half of 46 is 23, so the question no longer tests anything.

problems.detail: 'Meiosis makes four genetically different gametes' is not true for egg production. In human females, meiosis makes one egg and smaller polar bodies, not four gametes. The card says 'four cells', but the remember line turns this into four gametes. Saying 'four genetically different cells' would avoid the problem.
